setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Doll** (4 reviews): Garcia reached the high notes while the crowd willed him on; The Wheel flowed nicely into China Doll [17][22][25][26]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): In the Scarlet into Fire segment, Phil is right on time for the crossover; Scarlet into Fire is meticulously played, with Jerry finding a low riff on the theme [18][23][24]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (2 reviews): The transition from Half-Step into Franklin's Tower is cheerful, though the opening seemed to stretch on; Reviewer calls the opening Half-Step a disaster [18][20]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): Jerry takes big, searching, melodic turns after every verse, including the last, in a passionate, exploratory Fire; Jerry badly flubs the lyrics in Fire, worse than usual [19][20]
- **Lazy Lightnin'** (1 review): Lazy Lightning stands out as hot playing in the first set [20]
- **Deal** (1 review): Deal is tepid [24]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Band skipped the Scarlet reprise and went straight into Lost Sailor [22]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums are particularly powerful and lead into a spacey, beautiful Wheel [23]

## Setlist highlights

- **Wheel Prelude**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **encore call**: back after 155 archived shows (671 days); rare: 13 archived performances [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-03-10.nak700.glassberg.motb.82374.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 26 songs; 178 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1981-03-10.175117.sbd.miller.phase-repair.flac1644**: soundboard; 23 songs; 182 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd81-03-10.glassberg.wise.7630.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 180 min; rated 4.04/5 by 26 [6]. Said about its sound: Recording quality is mostly superb; Considered one of the best-sounding audience recordings; At the start of the feed there is a loud reverb-box thump; it sounds good by halfway [18][23][27]
- **gd1981-03-10.152637.nak500.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 177 min [7]

## Around the show

- Second set was structured with songs alternating between Jerry and Bob singers, with no breaks [22]
- Writer watched from a corporate box on Phil's side of the Garden [25]
- The writer hears the start of the end for Garcia's sweet 1970s voice, though the soul remained [17]
- Jerry seems off and the band loose compared with hot shows of 3/5 and 3/9 [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-03-10.nak700.glassberg.motb.82374.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert and C. Ladner; source: Nakamichi CM700's > Sony TC-D5M > MAC [1]. Also: Mastered with Adobe Audition 2.0, using Waves Z-Noise noise reduction learned from a blank tape patch, plus Izotope [1]
- **gd1981-03-10.175117.sbd.miller.phase-repair.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 13, 2025; source: SBD > Cassette Master > DAT (44.1k) [5]. Also: This version repairs a vocal phase issue found in the earlier soundboard transfer, shnid 115598 [5]
- **gd81-03-10.glassberg.wise.7630.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Nak CM700's [6]
- **gd1981-03-10.152637.nak500.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi DM-500 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII-S) [7]. Also: Barry Glassberg's front-of-board Nakamichi 700 source supplies a 24-second patch in Drums and all of Brokedown Palace [7]
